FINAL SUBMISSION — Answer: the Social domain (discipline == "Social").

Hypothesis (natural-language answer):
The domain in which both the original and the replication studies primarily used student subjects (original 82.4%, replication 80.9%) is the SOCIAL discipline — i.e. the social/personality-psychology studies coded `discipline == "Social"` in meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv. Counting one record per original study (n = 74 Social studies), 83.8% (62/74) of the original studies and 81.1% (60/74) of their replications used student subjects; counting every lab-level replication record (n = 668 Social records) the shares are 82.0% (548/668) original and 78.4% (524/668) replication. The other domains are clearly excluded on at least one side: Cognitive is 75.5%/81.6% (49 studies; 71.4%/83.8% by record) because its originals relied much more on "anyone"/community samples, and Economics is 94.4%/100.0% (18 studies) — both far above the quoted pair. No `project` value fits either (rpp 80.4/76.3, ml1 75.0/73.0, ml3 90.0/100.0, ee 94.4/100.0), consistent with `project` being a replication-project label rather than a domain. Residual uncertainty: no unit or subset reproduces 82.4%/80.9% exactly — the study-level Social figures are +1.4/+0.2 pts off (total absolute gap 1.6 pts, smallest of all candidates tested) and the record-level reading is -0.4/-2.5 pts off — so the identification of Social is robust while the exact decimal pair most likely comes from a marginally different unit/version of these data.

RESULTS TABLE (domain = `discipline`; student share = share coded "students" in `subjects.o` / `subjects.r`)

| domain | lab-level records n | orig students % (n) | repl students % (n) | unique studies n | orig students % (n) | repl students % (n) | total abs gap vs 82.4/80.9 (studies) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Social | 668 | 82.04 (548) | 78.44 (524) | 74 | 83.78 (62) | 81.08 (60) | 1.56 |
| Cognitive | 241 | 71.37 (172) | 83.82 (202) | 49 | 75.51 (37) | 81.63 (40) | 7.62 |
| Economics | 18 | 94.44 (17) | 100.00 (18) | 18 | 94.44 (17) | 100.00 (18) | 31.14 |

Runner-up grouping of any kind tested: `project == rpp` (80.41/76.29, gap 6.60) — worse, and not a domain.

Tie rule (study level): replication share uses the first row per `id`. 16 ids vary across labs in `subjects.r` (all are ml1 studies in which 27/37 labs used students), so first-row == majority-lab == "any lab used students" (Social replication stays 81.08%, 60/74); only a strict "all labs used students" rule moves it, down to 63.51% (47/74).

Sensitivity (caveat only, not headline; Social discipline): dropping `drop == True` rows gives 99.27/80.18 (records, n=550) and 93.75/85.94 (studies, n=64); removing `aggregated == True` rows gives 81.97/77.81 (records) and 83.78/81.08 (studies); complete-case on the core meta-regression variables gives 98.91/79.74 (records) and 91.04/83.58 (studies). These conventions move the numbers far from the quoted pair, which is why they were kept out of the headline rather than tuned to hit the digits.

File 2 (`meta-regression_replication_success_data_...csv`, 143 x 15) excluded: it has no subjects field at all and its only identifier is an initials+surname string that matches just 20/143 rows of file 1, so it can neither supply nor cross-check these shares.

payload.hypothesis: The domain is Social (discipline == "Social"). At the original-study level (one record per study, n = 74 Social studies) 83.8% (62/74) of original studies and 81.1% (60/74) of replications used student subjects, the closest match to the quoted 82.4% / 80.9%; at the lab-record level (n = 668 Social records) the shares are 82.0% (548/668) and 78.4% (524/668). Cognitive (75.5% / 81.6%, n = 49) and Economics (94.4% / 100.0%, n = 18) are excluded because at least one side is far from the quoted pair, and no `project` value fits (rpp 80.4/76.3, ml1 75.0/73.0, ml3 90.0/100.0, ee 94.4/100.0). Residual uncertainty: no subset reproduces 82.4/80.9 exactly (smallest total absolute gap 1.6 pts for Social at study level), so the domain identification is robust while the exact decimals likely reflect a slightly different unit/data version.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspected both staged CSVs; established that only file 1 carries subject types and that file 2 has no subjects field plus an unreliable name-based identifier (20/143 matches). 2) Defined domain = `discipline`; computed the share of `subjects.o == 'students'` and `subjects.r == 'students'` per discipline in two units: all 927 lab-level records and 141 unique original studies (dedup by `id`). 3) Reported the study-level replication tie rule (first row per id) and tested majority-lab / any-lab / all-lab alternatives (only all-lab changes the result). 4) Ranked every candidate grouping (discipline and project x both units, plus all combinations of the `drop`, `aggregated` and complete-case filters) by absolute deviation from the quoted 82.4/80.9 pair. 5) Kept drop/aggregated/complete-case as caveat columns rather than headline. 6) Headlined study-level Social 83.8%/81.1% (n=74) with row-level 82.0%/78.4% (n=668) as the alternative reading, stating the residual gap without tuning filters. Artifacts: analysis/final_analysis.py (executed), analysis/analysis_log.txt, analysis/results_by_discipline.csv, analysis/results_table.md, analysis/candidate_ranking.csv, analysis/sensitivity_social.csv.
